transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. It's like, I’ll start talking about an overnight shift at the hospital—I'm an orderly, and those night shifts get really weird sometimes, you know? Especially when it's raining. I actually used to play soccer in the rain a lot back in high school, which is crazy because the mud would get absolutely everywhere, and our uniforms were this awful bright yellow... kind of like the paint colors they use on the walls in the third-floor hallway at work. 

But yeah, I'll be trying to tell the nurses about the patient charts or something, and I just end up jumping from the overnight shift to soccer to paint colors, and... I can just see everyone getting completely lost while I'm talking. It's just getting really hard to explain things.
Are these difficulties with keeping your thoughts in order causing problems for you at work or in your relationships with others?

Yeah, it’s… it’s causing a lot of problems. At work, I’ve had to ask the other orderlies to double-check my rounds and my charting, because I just can't keep it straight. And charting is so specific, you know? They use these black binders, and you have to use a black pen—never blue, only black. I bought a pack of blue pens once by mistake, the kind with the little rubber grips on them, and they just sat in my drawer for months. I think my roommate finally threw them away. 

But yeah, at home, it’s bad too. I’m living with my roommate, but I’ve just… I’ve completely ignored my friends. I haven't paid any of my bills. The apartment is just a total mess, like, out of control. There's just stuff everywhere. And I guess it all just piled up, the mess and the charting and everything, because… well, employee health actually sent me for an emergency evaluation. I ended up telling them I was thinking about suicide. Which, you know, I guess is why I'm here. But I still don't know what happened to those blue pens.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Yeah, I guess... empty is a good word for it. Most days I just wake up and everything feels so heavy. Like I'm walking underwater or something. It's like that from the minute I open my eyes. And then after my shifts, I can't even start the car. I just sit in the driver's seat crying for... I don't even know how long, before I can drive home. My car is this old Honda Civic, actually. It’s got that weird smell, like old french fries and pine air freshener? I tried using one of those vanilla ones once, but it just made it worse, especially in the summer when the heat bakes it into the upholstery. The seats are cloth, not leather. Leather gets too hot anyway, you know? Like when you wear shorts and your legs stick to it. I hate that. But yeah, I just sit there and cry.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy or irritable for several days?

No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really felt happy at all, let alone abnormally happy. Or irritable, really. I mean, maybe a little annoyed when things go wrong, but not for days. Usually, I'm just too tired to be mad. Being mad takes a lot of energy, you know? Like when people yell, they get all red in the face and their veins pop out. My old soccer coach used to do that. Coach Miller. He was this huge guy, always wore these tight tracksuits that swished when he walked. Swish, swish, swish. It was so loud on the indoor turf. We had indoor practice during the winter because the ground would freeze solid. Once, a kid broke his arm falling on the frozen mud. Just snapped it right above the wrist. They had to call an ambulance, and the sirens were so loud... kind of like the sirens you hear from the ER bay when I'm taking out the trash at work. 

But no, I haven't had any days where I felt super happy or anything like that. Just... heavy.
How long have you been feeling this emptiness and heaviness?

I guess... it's been about a year and two months. Yeah, like 14 months of just this depression and total loss of interest in everything. I remember because it started right around the time my roommate moved in. He brought this giant, ugly green couch with him. It was one of those sleeper sofas, you know? The kind with the really thin mattress and that metal bar that digs right into your lower back if you try to sleep on it. We had to carry it up three flights of stairs because the elevator in our apartment building is always broken. The landlord keeps saying he's going to fix it, but he just puts up this shiny yellow caution tape across the doors. 

It's exactly like the tape they use at the hospital when there's a spill on the ward. Like when a patient drops a whole tray of pureed food. Pureed peas smell the absolute worst, honestly. They get all crusty on the linoleum if housekeeping doesn't mop it up right away. Housekeeping is always understaffed on Tuesdays for some reason, so sometimes I just grab the mop myself even though it's not really my job. The mop buckets are that same bright yellow as the caution tape. But yeah, it's been about a year and two months of feeling this heavy.
Have you had any thoughts of suicide recently, other than what you mentioned to employee health?

Well, yeah. I mean, especially after the really bad nights on the ward. Sometimes I just keep thinking that it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up at all. And then sometimes the thought comes that I should just... just end it. It gets really loud in my head. I get so scared when that happens, so I usually end up telling someone, like my supervisor or employee health. 

Employee health is down in the basement of the hospital, right next to the laundry room. It's always so hot down there because of the massive industrial dryers they use for the bedsheets. The sheets are this stark white, but they get super scratchy after being washed so many times. I always feel bad for the patients who have to sleep on them, especially the ones with sensitive skin. My mom has really sensitive skin. She can only use this one specific brand of oatmeal soap, otherwise she breaks out in these awful red hives. The soap comes in this little cardboard box with a picture of a wheat stalk on it. It smells exactly like the oatmeal cookies my grandma used to bake when I was a kid. She'd always put raisins in them, which I hated. Raisins are just ruined grapes, you know? Why ruin a perfectly good grape? 

But yeah, I do get those thoughts about ending it, and it scares me.
Do you find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before feeling this emptiness and heaviness?

No, not really. I used to do a lot of stuff, actually. I'd sketch out these big ideas for murals... I always wanted to paint one on the side of this old brick building near my place. The bricks are that really deep, faded red, almost like dried blood, you know? They have all these chips and cracks in them from the weather. The winters here are so brutal on the masonry. The salt they put down on the sidewalks just eats right through the concrete. It gets all powdery and white, and it ruins your shoes. I had this pair of black boots that got completely destroyed by the salt last year. They were my favorite boots, too. They had these thick rubber soles that were perfect for walking on the wet floors at the hospital. 

But yeah, the sketching... it just feels completely pointless now. I don't even open my sketchbook. I used to cook for my friends a lot, too, and we'd play soccer on the weekends. We'd go to the park by the river. There's this huge willow tree there with branches that hang all the way down to the water. The ducks always hide under it when it rains. Mallards, mostly. The males have those bright green heads that look almost metallic in the sun. It's weird how birds have such bright colors but mammals are mostly just brown and gray. Except for mandrills, I guess. They have those crazy blue and red faces. I saw one at the zoo when I was a kid, and it just stared at me through the glass. It was kind of unsettling, honestly. 

But now... I don't know. I don't care about soccer or cooking. I usually just ignore my friends' messages and stay in my apartment. It's just easier to stay inside.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past 14 months?

Yeah, I have. I barely get hungry anymore, honestly. Most days I just drink coffee at work, maybe grab some of those vending-machine crackers if my stomach starts hurting. The crackers are always the peanut butter ones, but the peanut butter is so dry and crumbly. It gets stuck to the roof of your mouth and you have to drink like a gallon of water just to swallow it. The water fountain by the vending machines on the third floor has this weird metallic taste to it anyway. I think the pipes are super old. The maintenance guy, Gary, he said the building was built in the seventies and they never updated the plumbing. Gary wears these heavy denim overalls every single day. I don't know how he doesn't overheat, especially when he has to fix the radiators. The radiators hiss so loud in the winter, it sounds like a bunch of angry snakes trapped in the walls. I hate snakes. My cousin had a pet python once and it got loose in his house for three weeks. They finally found it curled up behind the dryer, just soaking up the heat. Dryers get so hot, like the ones in the hospital laundry room I was talking about. 

But yeah, my clothes have gotten really loose. I had to punch an extra hole in my belt just to keep my work pants from falling down.
Are there any activities that you still find enjoyable or that you look forward to?

No, not really. Like I said before, I used to do all that stuff... sketching out those big mural ideas, cooking for my friends, playing soccer on the weekends. But now, it all just feels completely pointless. I don't look forward to any of it. I usually just ignore my friends when they message me and stay in my apartment. My apartment is on the fourth floor, and the elevator has been broken for like three months. The landlord keeps saying he's going to get a part shipped in from Germany or something, but I think he's just cheap. He drives this massive, shiny black SUV, one of those ones with the tinted windows so you can't see who's inside. It always takes up two parking spots in the lot. People who double-park are the worst, especially when it snows and the plows can't get through properly. The snow plows here are huge, they have these massive yellow blades that scrape against the asphalt and make this horrible screeching noise. It wakes me up at like 4 AM every time it snows. I can never get back to sleep after that screeching sound. It just echoes in my head. But yeah, I don't really enjoy anything anymore, I just stay inside.
Do you find that you're moving more slowly than usual?

Yeah, my mom actually mentioned that the other day. She said I look like I'm moving underwater. It feels like that, too, like the air is just thick and heavy. But then... then there are times where I just can't stop moving. Like, I can't sit still at all. I'll just pace back and forth in my apartment for hours, or I'll sit there rubbing my hands together so much that the skin gets all raw and sore. My hands get really dry in the winter anyway, especially with all the hand sanitizer we have to use at the hospital. They have those dispensers mounted on the walls outside every single patient room, and the sanitizer smells like cheap vodka. It stings if you have even a tiny paper cut. I got a paper cut last week from opening a box of new bedsheets for the supply closet. The sheets are always so stiff and scratchy when they're brand new, they have to be washed like five times before they actually feel soft. The laundry room down in the basement of the hospital is always so humid because of the giant industrial washers they use. They have these heavy metal doors that lock shut, kind of like a submarine hatch. I watched this documentary about submarines once, about how the pressure gets so intense the deeper they go that the whole metal hull actually shrinks. It's crazy to think about being trapped in a metal tube that deep underwater, with no light and just the sound of the sonar pinging. Ping... ping... it's kind of a lonely sound. But yeah, sometimes I'm super slow, and other times I'm just pacing and rubbing my hands until they hurt.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

I don't really know if I feel anxious. I mean, I guess I worry about things sometimes, but not like a constant panic or anything. Mostly my mind is just... blank, or focused on the wrong stuff. Like yesterday, I spent probably two hours just staring at the scuff marks on the linoleum floor in the hallway outside my apartment. The linoleum is this gross beige color, and it's peeling up in the corners near the baseboards. The baseboards are supposed to be white, but they're covered in this layer of grime that looks like it hasn't been cleaned since the nineties. I tried scrubbing it once with this lemon-scented cleaner I bought at the dollar store, but the smell was so overpowering it gave me a massive headache. The dollar store is only a couple of blocks from my place, right next to this old diner that sells the greasiest fries. The fries always come in those little red plastic baskets lined with wax paper. The wax paper gets completely translucent from all the oil. It's kind of gross if you think about it too much, all that grease just soaking through. But yeah, I don't think I'm super anxious or anything, just... I don't know, tired, I guess.
Do you ever have days where you feel slightly more interested in the things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. Even on what you'd call a "good" day, it's just... nothing. Like I told you earlier, I used to do all that stuff, you know? Sketching out those big mural ideas in my notebook, cooking meals for my friends, playing soccer on the weekends... but now it all just feels completely pointless. I don't care about any of it. I usually just ignore my friends when they message me and stay in my apartment. My phone is always on silent anyway because the notification sound I picked is really annoying. It's this weird chirping noise, kind of like a cricket but electronic. I heard real crickets can tell you the temperature if you count their chirps, which is pretty wild. You just count how many times they chirp in 14 seconds and add 40, and that's the temperature in Fahrenheit. Fahrenheit is such a weird system when you think about it. The rest of the world uses Celsius, which makes way more sense because water freezes at zero and boils at a hundred. A hundred is a nice, round number. I used to try and collect exactly a hundred bottle caps when I was a kid. I'd find them all over the park near my house. The park had this really old wooden playground equipment that gave you splinters if you weren't careful. But yeah, no... I don't ever feel interested in those things anymore. I just stay in my apartment.
Have you had any days recently where you felt even slightly better or more hopeful than you have been?

No... no, I haven't. Most days, it's just... I wake up and I immediately feel this heaviness. Like I'm completely empty, but also weighed down at the same time. It's like that all day, especially at work. After my shifts at the hospital, I'll just sit in my car in the parking garage and start crying. I can't even start the engine to drive home for, like, twenty minutes. My car is this old Honda Civic, the paint is chipping off the hood in these big flakes that look like puzzle pieces. The pieces always remind me of this jigsaw puzzle I tried to do with my mom when I was a kid. It was a picture of a hot air balloon festival, but all the sky pieces were the exact same shade of blue. It took us weeks to finish it, and we left it on the dining room table the whole time. We had to eat dinner on the couch watching TV because the table was covered in puzzle pieces. We used to watch those game shows where people have to guess the price of groceries. It's crazy how expensive cereal has gotten lately. I saw a box of cornflakes at the store the other day and it was almost seven dollars. Seven dollars for baked corn. Corn is actually a grass, not a vegetable, which is weird to think about. Like, you're just eating grass seeds. But yeah, I just sit in the car and cry. I don't feel hopeful at all.
Are there any small things that still bring you a bit of joy or pleasure?

No... nothing really brings me any joy anymore. I know I mentioned it before, but I used to do all sorts of things. I'd sketch out these big mural ideas, cook dinners for my friends, play soccer on the weekends... but now? It just feels completely pointless. I don't even want to try. I just ignore my friends' messages and stay in my apartment. My apartment gets so hot in the afternoon because the windows face west. The blinds don't really block out the sun, they just kind of slice the light into these harsh yellow lines across the floor. I tried taping up some cardboard over the window in my bedroom once, but it kept falling down because the tape wasn't sticky enough. It was that cheap masking tape, the kind that feels almost like paper. Paper is made from trees, obviously, but I read once that you can make paper out of elephant poop. They wash it and boil it or something, and then press it into sheets. It's supposed to be really eco-friendly. I wonder if it smells bad, though. Probably not if they boil it. Boiling water kills all the bacteria, right? That's why you're supposed to boil water if you're out camping and you run out of bottled water. I went camping once when I was a kid and got completely covered in mosquito bites. But yeah, no... I don't get any pleasure out of anything these days. I just stay inside.
Do you still enjoy any small pleasures in life, like taking a warm bath or reading a book?

No, not really... I know I've said this already, but it's like all those things I used to love just... they don't mean anything now. Like the sketching, cooking for people, the weekend soccer games... it all just feels completely pointless. I don't even have the energy for a bath or a book. I usually just ignore my phone when my friends message me and stay in my apartment. My phone battery is actually almost dead right now because I lost my charging cable. It's one of those braided ones, you know? They're supposed to be tougher, but the cat I had growing up used to chew through every cord in the house. His name was Barnaby. He was an orange tabby, and they say orange cats all share one brain cell, which I think is pretty funny. Barnaby used to sit on top of the refrigerator and just stare at the ceiling for hours. I wonder what he was looking at. Maybe he saw a ghost. People say animals can see things we can't, like changes in the magnetic field or whatever. Birds use the magnetic field to migrate thousands of miles every year. It's crazy how they just know where to go without a map. I get lost trying to find a new room at the hospital where I work. But yeah... I don't enjoy anything like that anymore. I just stay in my apartment.
Do you feel like you're moving slower or faster than usual most of the time?

I don't know, it's kind of both, I guess. People at the hospital tell me I move like I'm underwater lately, just really slow and heavy. But then other times, I can't sit still at all. I'll just keep pacing back and forth in my apartment, or I'll sit there rubbing my hands together over and over until the skin is actually sore. I used to get sore hands a lot when I played soccer because I was the goalie for a while. Goalie gloves are so thick, but they still don't stop the sting if someone kicks the ball really hard. Professional goalies must have crazy strong hands. I saw a video once of a guy crushing an apple with one hand. Apples are supposed to wake you up better than coffee in the morning because of the natural sugars. I tried that once, but I just ended up with a stomach ache. My mom used to make this baked apple dessert with cinnamon and oats on top. Cinnamon comes from the bark of a tree, which is wild. Like, who first decided to peel a tree and eat the bark? People must have been really hungry back then. But yeah... I either move like I'm underwater or I'm pacing around rubbing my hands raw.
Do you think your movement and reaction time have been significantly slower than normal most of the time over the past 14 months?

Yeah, like I was just saying... people at work tell me I move like I'm underwater. Just really, really slow. But it's not all the time, because sometimes I get this feeling and I just can't sit still. I'll pace around my apartment for hours, or I just sit there rubbing my hands together over and over until they're actually raw and sore. I don't even realize I'm doing it until it hurts. Pain is a weird thing, isn't it? It's just a signal your brain sends to tell you something is wrong, but sometimes the brain gets it wrong. Like phantom limb pain. I read about this guy who lost his arm in a motorcycle accident and he still felt like his hand was clenching too tight. They treated him with a mirror box, which tricks the brain into thinking the arm is still there so you can unclench it. Mirrors are creepy sometimes. If you stare into a mirror in a dark room for too long, your brain starts distorting your face and you see monsters. It's called the Troxler effect. It's just an optical illusion, but it's used in a lot of horror movies. I hate horror movies. They just rely on jump scares instead of actual psychological tension. But anyway... yeah, I either move super slow or I'm pacing and rubbing my hands.
Do you think your slowed movement is noticeable to others most of the time?

Yeah, I mean, I know I keep saying this, but they definitely notice. The nurses and the other aides at the hospital are the ones who actually tell me I'm moving like I'm underwater. So it's obvious to them. But the other part... the not being able to sit still, pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands together till they're sore... I don't know if people at work see that, because I mostly do it when I'm alone at home. 

My downstairs neighbor definitely notices the pacing, though. He banged on the ceiling with a broom handle the other night. Brooms are such a weird invention if you really think about it. It's literally just straw tied to a stick, but we still use them even though we have vacuums now. Vacuums are so loud, though. My mom had this old Hoover when I was a kid that sounded like a jet engine taking off. Jets are terrifying. The idea of being in a metal tube miles up in the sky just relying on air pressure... it makes no sense to me. The Wright brothers were just bicycle mechanics, you know? They went from fixing bike chains to inventing human flight. I used to ride a bike to the hospital for my shifts, but it got a flat tire a few months ago and I never bothered to fix it. Bicycles are actually really efficient machines. But yeah, the people at work definitely notice when I'm moving slow.
Do you feel that your depressive symptoms are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Yeah, it's... it's definitely messing everything up. At the hospital, I've had to have my coworkers double-check my rounds and my charting because I just can't focus. And at home, it's worse. I've completely fallen behind on my bills, I haven't texted any of my friends back in weeks, and my apartment is just... it's a disaster zone right now. There's trash everywhere. I used to be really good at keeping things clean, you know? My mom always made me do chores on Saturday mornings. We had this chore chart with little gold stars. Gold stars are such a weird way to motivate kids. Like, it's just a shiny piece of paper, but you'd do anything for it. Paper is actually made from trees, which is crazy when you think about how thin it is. They have to mash the wood into pulp and press it. I saw a documentary about a paper mill once, and the smell is supposed to be awful, like rotten eggs. Rotten eggs have sulfur in them. Sulfur is what they use in matches, too. I used to collect matchbooks from different restaurants when I was little, but most places don't even have them anymore because nobody smokes inside. But anyway, yeah... it got so bad that employee health actually sent me for an emergency evaluation because I... I told them I was thinking about suicide. So, yeah, it's interfering with everything.
Do you feel like your depressive symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

Yeah, it's... it's not just the last two weeks, honestly. The feeling like everything is pointless, the depression, not caring about anything... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It just drags on and on. Time is so weird like that. When you're miserable, a year feels like a decade, but when you're having fun, a year is gone in a blink. Einstein talked about relativity like that, right? Like time actually moves differently depending on how fast you're going. Space travel would completely mess with your age. You could go on a ship at light speed and come back and everyone you know is dead. That's so depressing to think about. I watched this movie once where they went through a wormhole and one guy stayed on the ship, and when they came back he had aged like twenty years while they only aged a few hours. He just had to sit there alone for twenty years. Being alone for that long would break anybody's brain. But yeah... the depression has been going on for like 14 months now.

doctor.intent: determine presence of manic or hypomanic episodes

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of a manic or hypomanic episode (feeling abnormally happy or irritable), which is not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really felt happy at all, let alone abnormally happy. Or irritable, really. I mean, maybe a little annoyed when things go wrong, but not for days. Usually, I'm just too tired to be mad. Being mad takes a lot of energy, you know? Like when people yell, they get all red in the face and their veins pop out. My old soccer coach used to do that. Coach Miller. He was this huge guy, always wore these tight tracksuits that swished when he walked. Swish, swish, swish. It was so loud on the indoor turf. We had indoor practice during the winter because the ground would freeze solid. Once, a kid broke his arm falling on the frozen mud. Just snapped it right above the wrist. They had to call an ambulance, and the sirens were so loud... kind of like the sirens you hear from the ER bay when I'm taking out the trash at work. 

But no, I haven't had any days where I felt super happy or anything like that. Just... heavy.

I had this pair of black boots that got completely destroyed by the salt last year. They were my favorite boots, too. They had these thick rubber soles that were perfect for walking on the wet floors at the hospital. 

But yeah, the sketching... it just feels completely pointless now. I don't even open my sketchbook. I used to cook for my friends a lot, too, and we'd play soccer on the weekends. We'd go to the park by the river. There's this huge willow tree there with branches that hang all the way down to the water. The ducks always hide under it when it rains. Mallards, mostly. The males have those bright green heads that look almost metallic in the sun. It's weird how birds have such bright colors but mammals are mostly just brown and gray. Except for mandrills, I guess. They have those crazy blue and red faces. I saw one at the zoo when I was a kid, and it just stared at me through the glass. It was kind of unsettling, honestly.

The water fountain by the vending machines on the third floor has this weird metallic taste to it anyway. I think the pipes are super old. The maintenance guy, Gary, he said the building was built in the seventies and they never updated the plumbing. Gary wears these heavy denim overalls every single day. I don't know how he doesn't overheat, especially when he has to fix the radiators. The radiators hiss so loud in the winter, it sounds like a bunch of angry snakes trapped in the walls. I hate snakes. My cousin had a pet python once and it got loose in his house for three weeks. They finally found it curled up behind the dryer, just soaking up the heat. Dryers get so hot, like the ones in the hospital laundry room I was talking about. 

But yeah, my clothes have gotten really loose. I had to punch an extra hole in my belt just to keep my work pants from falling down.

I got a paper cut last week from opening a box of new bedsheets for the supply closet. The sheets are always so stiff and scratchy when they're brand new, they have to be washed like five times before they actually feel soft. The laundry room down in the basement of the hospital is always so humid because of the giant industrial washers they use. They have these heavy metal doors that lock shut, kind of like a submarine hatch. I watched this documentary about submarines once, about how the pressure gets so intense the deeper they go that the whole metal hull actually shrinks. It's crazy to think about being trapped in a metal tube that deep underwater, with no light and just the sound of the sonar pinging. Ping... ping... it's kind of a lonely sound. But yeah, sometimes I'm super slow, and other times I'm just pacing and rubbing my hands until they hurt.

I read about this guy who lost his arm in a motorcycle accident and he still felt like his hand was clenching too tight. They treated him with a mirror box, which tricks the brain into thinking the arm is still there so you can unclench it. Mirrors are creepy sometimes. If you stare into a mirror in a dark room for too long, your brain starts distorting your face and you see monsters. It's called the Troxler effect. The idea of being in a metal tube miles up in the sky just relying on air pressure... it makes no sense to me. The Wright brothers were just bicycle mechanics, you know? Gold stars are such a weird way to motivate kids. Like, it's just a shiny piece of paper, but you'd do anything for it. Paper is actually made from trees, which is crazy when you think about how thin it is. They have to mash the wood into pulp and press it. I saw a documentary about a paper mill once, and the smell is supposed to be awful, like rotten eggs. Rotten eggs have sulfur in them. Sulfur is what they use in matches, too. I used to collect matchbooks from different restaurants when I was little, but most places don't even have them anymore because nobody smokes inside. But anyway, yeah... it got so bad that employee health actually sent me for an emergency evaluation because I... I told them I was thinking about suicide. So, yeah, it's interfering with everything.

Like time actually moves differently depending on how fast you're going. Space travel would completely mess with your age. You could go on a ship at light speed and come back and everyone you know is dead. That's so depressing to think about. I watched this movie once where they went through a wormhole and one guy stayed on the ship, and when they came back he had aged like twenty years while they only aged a few hours.
